profile.summary: DeepFoldRNA predicts the 3D (tertiary) structure of an RNA from its sequence alone. It builds a multiple sequence alignment and secondary structure prediction for the input RNA, uses a deep self-attention network to predict distance and angle restraints, and then folds the chain by gradient-based simulation. The output is all-atom models in PDB format, before and after refinement.

summary_quotes.text: We developed DeepFoldRNA to predict RNA structures from sequence alone by coupling deep self-attention neural networks with gradient-based folding simulations.
Will output the generated MSA (seq.afa), predicted secondary structure (ss.txt), hidden Markov model (seq.cm), and the predicted torsion angles
the unrefined full atom models will be saved as unrefined_model.pdb, while the refined models will be saved as refined_model.pdb

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: The pipeline has four stages. First, rMSA builds an MSA and PETfold predicts secondary structure; SPOT-RNA-1D predicts torsion angles. Second, a neural network with 48 MSA transformer blocks, 4 single-sequence blocks and 2 pair blocks, run for 4 recycling cycles, predicts restraints: binned distances from 2 to 40 Angstrom, inter-residue orientation angles and torsion angles. Third, gradient-based folding simulations build the structure from these restraints. Fourth, SimRNA and QRNAS refine the full-atom model. The authors note that the restraints do not include base atoms, so the unrefined model has slightly better backbone RMSD but worse base pairing than the refined one.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The stand-alone program is Version 1.0, dated 03/28/2022. The network weights are stored in the repository under network/parameters, in four folders (model_1, model_1_2, model_2, model_2_2) of three weight files each. By default the program makes 6 models with different network parameters, or 3 if --generate_all_models is False. Results also depend on the sequence databases used for MSA generation. A result should name the commit (this page read 0c2c1925), the model number and whether the refined or unrefined model was used. A web server is also available.

run_guide.summary: Install DeepFoldRNA, its third-party tools and sequence databases at a pinned commit, then predict the 3D structure of one RNA sequence.
prerequisites: An x86_64 Linux machine with more than 500 GB of free disk, mostly for the sequence databases.
The conda environment pins python=3.7 and pytorch 1.10. A GPU is used automatically if available; GPU type and memory are not stated.
Non-commercial use only (PolyForm Noncommercial per the README); the third-party tools have their own licences.

steps.title: Get the code at the pinned commit
steps.shell:
git clone https://github.com/robpearc/DeepFoldRNA.git
cd DeepFoldRNA
git checkout --detach 0c2c1925c95002abd5ade51f57bfb52271105298
steps.explanation: The README gives no clone command; these lines are added to get the commit this page was written from. Later steps run from this package directory.

steps.shell:

pip install -r bin/SPOT-RNA-1D/requirements.txt

steps.title: Install the sequence databases
steps.explanation: Downloads and processes the databases for MSA generation into bin/rMSA/database. This needs more than 500 GB and may take hours.

quotes.text: ./scripts/install_sequence_database.sh
The sequence databases will be saved at <package_dir>/bin/rMSA/database

steps.title: Predict a structure
steps.shell:
source scripts/activate_conda_env.sh
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1
mkdir -p example_input
printf '>5v17A\nGGAUCAACCCCAGGUGUGGCACACCAGUCAUACCUUGAUCC\n' > example_input/seq.fasta
python3 runDeepFoldRNA.py --input_dir example_input
steps.explanation: Activates the environment, sets one thread as the README advises, writes the README's example sequence to seq.fasta and runs the pipeline. The directory name example_input and the mkdir and printf lines are added to create the input file the README describes.
